# 13 — The exit gate: seven Digests read and judged

**What to build:** nothing. This is the reading exercise that decides whether the Digest is worth
sustaining a habit around, which no automated case can answer.

The bar is the worked example in the parent spec. If a real Digest reads worse than that one, the problem
is composition rather than scope, and the response is to tune the prompt and cut length rather than to
add features. The parent spec says the Digest has to be good enough by roughly day four to keep the
capturing habit alive, so this reading is the gate and not a formality.

**Blocked by:** 03 — The Health Canary; 05 — A day that passed unread is still caught up; 07 — A rule
that fires on no day, and `reads::` as the thing you check; 08 — `handled::` names an occurrence, not
the day you spoke; 10 — Date Requests; 11 — The Digest reads the Standing Rules file; 12 — The Digest
asks phase 3's held-back questions, and counts the asking.

**Status:** completed

**Completed at:** 2026-09-02T10:44:32Z

- [ ] Every automated case in the phase 4 spec passes, and each one drives the scheduled run's single
      entry point.
- [ ] Manual: read seven consecutive real Digests and judge them against the parent spec's worked example.
- [ ] Manual: put a birthday twelve days out with a real Card behind it, and judge whether the suggestion
      is grounded in what was actually said.
- [ ] Manual: set a monthly rule and a weekly rule by hand, run the clock forward on the real box for a
      week, and confirm the days are right.
- [ ] Manual: hand-edit a rule into nonsense, confirm the Canary catches it and the run still completes.
- [ ] Manual: turn the model API off at Digest time and confirm a Canary-only message arrives.
- [ ] Manual: write a Standing Rule asking for shorter wording and confirm the next Digest changes.
- [ ] Seven real Digests have been read and judged worth reading. Then phase 5 starts.
